open_points.subject: M15 vs A05 fan-in rule for multiple delivering edges
open_points.text: M15: "the proof refuses two edges that can both deliver to one input port of cardinality `one`." A05 phase 6: "no two edges that can both deliver ... end at the same port, whatever its cardinality."
open_points.question: Should two edges that can both deliver into the same `many` input be allowed or always refused?
options: Allow for `many` inputs, refuse only for `one` inputs (M15 wording)
open_points.default_guess: Refuse for all cardinalities, following accepted decision A05.

open_points.subject: Operation pre-send refusal and attempt numbering
open_points.text: A09 rule 6: pre-send check failures conclude `operation_failed` and "no EffectAttempt exists". A11 rule 1: `attempt_number` advances on "each start of a send ...; nothing else takes one."
open_points.question: When an operation fails before send (binding stale/invalid target/input placement), does that NodeExecution consume an `attempt_number`, and if so by what rule?
options: Yes, assign the next `attempt_number` even without EffectAttempt
No, do not consume an attempt number for pre-send refusal
Use a fixed number (e.g., 1) for all pre-send refusals
open_points.default_guess: Consume the next attempt number so NodeExecution remains consistently ordered per node element.

open_points.subject: A09 request-building for file inputs on non-POST/PUT/PATCH methods
open_points.text: A09 rule 2 defines multipart for file inputs only "for `POST`, `PUT` and `PATCH`"; for "other methods" it says inputs form one JSON object body; proposal checks also say "for other methods any schema is accepted."
open_points.question: If a binding uses a method outside POST/PUT/PATCH and has a `file` input, is proposal/refusal behavior defined, and what body encoding must be used?
options: Refuse such bindings at proposal time
Allow and require multipart for any method with file input
Allow and encode file another way (e.g., base64 JSON)
open_points.default_guess: Refuse proposal when method is not POST/PUT/PATCH and any input port is `file`.

open_points.subject: A13 mapped-node execution order relative to other ready nodes
open_points.text: A13 rule 2: "The next node is the ready node with the smallest `node_id`... A mapped node runs its elements in list order; an element that waits does not stop the elements after it."
open_points.question: After one mapped element concludes (or waits), must execution continue with the same node’s next element immediately, or reselect the next ready node globally by `node_id` each step?
options: Process all remaining ready elements of that mapped node before reconsidering other nodes
After each element, re-run global node selection by smallest ready `node_id`
open_points.default_guess: After each element, re-run global ready-node selection to preserve one uniform scheduler rule.

open_points.subject: Agent view of personal_data fields
open_points.text: K-14: agent gets personal data "as digest and class"; A07 rule 4 says the surface returns "`value_id`, digest and class instead."
open_points.question: For personal_data returned to an agent, is `value_id` part of the allowed projection or must responses contain only digest and class?
options: Return value_id plus digest and class
open_points.default_guess: Return value_id, digest, and class, treating value_id as a non-content reference.
